name: Thompson Central Park New York
positioning: Midtown Manhattan hotel on 56th Street at the south edge of Central Park, formerly The Parker, with midcentury interiors by Thomas Juul-Hansen
best_for: Travelers who want a Midtown base a short walk from Central Park, Carnegie Hall and MoMA
Guests who want high-floor Upper Stories rooms with lounge access
Diners who want Indian Accent, Parker's and Burger Joint under one roof

facts.text: The hotel is on 56th Street at the south edge of Central Park, a short walk to Carnegie Hall and MoMA.
The property was formerly The Parker and became a Thompson hotel in 2019.
The hotel closed during the pandemic for a thorough facelift and reopened in November 2021 as Thompson Central Park.
The sleek, midcentury-feeling interiors were designed by Thomas Juul-Hansen.
At Indian Accent, Chef Manish Mehrotra puts an inventive spin on classic Indian dishes.
Parker's serves sharable dishes and inventive cocktails with live music.
Burger Joint has graffitied walls and a no-frills hamburgers and fries menu.
In-room dining is available around the clock.
Upper Stories rooms and suites are on the hotel's topmost guest floors, with access to the Upper Stories Lounge on the third floor.
Upper Stories rooms include private check-in, a Dyson Supersonic hair dryer and a Nespresso Vertuo.
Rooms have 400-thread-count Italian linens and midcentury finishes.
The exhale spa offers 60- and 90-minute massages, facials and body treatments.

highlights.text: Burger Joint is hidden behind a red curtain near reception, with a neon-lit burger above its entrance.
Upper Stories rooms have their own Victrola record players.
exhale has a daily schedule of barre, yoga and HIIT classes alongside a fitness center.

considerations.text: A daily destination fee is applied to each room, subject to change.
Parking is by valet at the hotel entrance, without in-and-out privileges.
Burger Joint takes walk-ins and does not accept reservations.
